images.title: The remainder chain of 1 ÷ 7
images.purpose: Show the remainders of 1 ÷ 7 as a closed loop, 1, 3, 2, 6, 4, 5 and back to 1, with the quotient digit made at each step.
images.composition: A ring of six circles in the centre joined by arrows, with the quotient line under the ring; generous white space around.
exact_structure: 6 circles arranged in a ring, clockwise from the top: 1, 3, 2, 6, 4, 5; circles outlined teal #0072B2; the top circle 1 filled reddish purple #CC79A7 as the start.
6 grey #6B7280 arrows clockwise: 1 to 3, 3 to 2, 2 to 6, 6 to 4, 4 to 5, and 5 back to 1.
Beside each arrow, a small amber #E69F00 quotient digit: 1 on 1 to 3, 4 on 3 to 2, 2 on 2 to 6, 8 on 6 to 4, 5 on 4 to 5, 7 on 5 to 1.
rejection: remainders in any order other than 1, 3, 2, 6, 4, 5
quotient digits on the arrows other than 1, 4, 2, 8, 5, 7 in that order
the loop not closing back to 1
images.takeaway: Dividing by 7 the only remainders are 1 to 6, so one must come back, and then the digits 142857 repeat.
images.description: A ring of remainders 1, 3, 2, 6, 4, 5 joined by arrows carrying the quotient digits 1, 4, 2, 8, 5, 7, above 1 ÷ 7 = 0.142857142857...
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video on 1 ÷ 7.
images.teaching_notes: Ask students to go round the ring reading the amber digits to rebuild the quotient.

image_decisions.why: The cycle of remainders is clearest as a closed loop.
